steps.note: Roll the app so new guest orders store '' instead of NULL. The column is still nullable, so old and new pods can run side by side during the rolling update.
Let any request that was still in flight on an old pod finish and commit.

Add CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID: catalog-only, but needs a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. Take it with a 200 ms lock_timeout and retry, so app queries never queue behind it for long. From here on no new NULL can be written.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Backfill: set email = '' only where it is NULL (the guest orders), in id ranges of 100,000 rows with a commit after each, so transactions and row locks stay short. The app never updates orders, so it never waits on these row locks. Rows that already have an email are not touched.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE lo bigint := 0; maxid bigint; BEGIN SELECT coalesce(max(id), 0) INTO maxid FROM orders; WHILE lo < maxid LOOP UPDATE orders SET email = '' WHERE id > lo AND id <= lo + 100000 AND email IS NULL; COMMIT; lo := lo + 100000; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.02); END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Validate the check constraint. This scans the table under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block reads or writes. It fails (and stops the plan, with nothing broken) if any NULL is left.
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null;

steps.note: SET NOT NULL. Postgres sees the valid CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) and skips the full-table scan, so the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock lasts only a moment. Same lock_timeout and retry as before.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN email SET NOT NULL; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Drop the helper CHECK constraint now that the column itself is NOT NULL (brief lock, same retry).
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; END $$;
